questions.question: As of October 2023, who is the central vigilance commissioner of India?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Praveen Kumar Srivastava**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• Central Vigilance Commission is the apex vigilance institution, free of control from any executive authority, monitoring all vigilance activity under the Central Government and advising various authorities in Central Government organizations in planning, executing, reviewing, and reforming their vigilance work.
 
• Vigilance means to ensure clean and prompt administrative action towards achieving efficiency and effectiveness of the employees in particular and the organization in general, as lack of Vigilance leans to waste, losses, and economic decline.
 
• The CVC was set up by the Government in February 1964 on the recommendations of the Committee on Prevention of Corruption, headed by Shri K. Santhanam. In 2003, the Parliament enacted CVC Act conferring statutory status on the CVC.
 
• The CVC is not controlled by any Ministry/Department. It is an independent body that is only responsible to the Parliament.
 
• The CVC receives complaints on corruption or misuse of office and to recommends appropriate action.

questions.question: The Census of 1881 which was undertaken on 17th February, 1881 by ______.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __W.C. Plowden__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The first synchronous census in India was conducted in the year 1881.
 
• This census was conducted under the guidance of W.C. Plowden, the then Census Commissioner of India.
 
• The synchronous census involved collecting demographic data at the same time across the entire country, making it a significant step in systematic data collection.
 
• It laid the foundation for modern population studies and data analysis in India.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Terminology:

 
 
• Census: A census is an official count or survey of a population, typically recording various details of individuals.
 
• Synchronous Census: This refers to a census where data is collected simultaneously across different regions at a specific point in time, ensuring consistency and comparability of data.
 
• Demographic Data: This includes information about the population such as age, sex, occupation, and other statistics that describe the characteristics of the population.
 
• Census Commissioner: An official responsible for overseeing the execution of the census operations in a country.
 
 
 
• Historical Context:
 
 
• The 1881 census marked the first comprehensive attempt to conduct a simultaneous census across British India.
 
• Prior to 1881, various regions conducted local censuses, but they were not coordinated or standardized.
 
• The 1881 census provided critical data that helped in the planning and administration of the British Indian Empire.
 
• This census set a precedent for future censuses, which have been conducted decennially (every ten years) in India.
 
 
 
• Significance:
 
 
• Conducting a synchronous census helps in obtaining accurate and reliable demographic data, which is crucial for policy making and governance.
 
• It aids in the allocation of resources, planning of social services, and implementation of various development programs.
 
• The data collected can be used for historical analysis and research on population trends and changes over time.
 
 
 
• Modern Censuses:
 
 
• The most recent census in India was conducted in 2011, and the next census is planned for 2021, although it may be delayed due to the COVID-19 pandemic.
 
• Modern censuses use advanced technology and methodologies to ensure accuracy and efficiency in data collection and analysis.

questions.question: Prime Minister Narendra Modi inaugurated the National Sickle Cell Anemia Elimination Mission 2047 in Lalpur village of _______ (July 2023).
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Madhya Pradesh**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

National Sickle Cell Anaemia Elimination Mission (NSCEM): 

 
• The National Sickle Cell Anaemia Elimination Program, introduced in the Union Budget 2023, focuses on addressing the significant health challenges posed by sickle cell disease, particularly among tribal populations of the country.
 
• Sickle cell disease (SCD) is a chronic single gene disorder causing a debilitating systemic syndrome characterized by chronic anemia, acute painful episodes, organ infarction and chronic organ damage and by a significant reduction in life expectancy. 
 
• Implemented in 17 high-focus states across the country, this program aims to improve the care and prospects of all sickle cell disease patients while reducing the prevalence of the disease.
 
• The 17 states are- Gujarat, Maharashtra, Rajasthan, Madhya Pradesh, Jharkhand, Chhattisgarh, West Bengal, Odisha, Tamil Nadu, Telangana, Andhra Pradesh, Karnataka, Assam, Uttar Pradesh, Kerala, Bihar, and Uttarakhand.
 
• The program is executed in a mission mode as part of the National Health Mission (NHM), aims to eliminate sickle cell genetic transmission by the year 2047, showing a long-term commitment to eradicating the disease.
 
• Over a period of three years, spanning from the fiscal year 2023-24 to 2025-26, the program targets screening approximately 7.0 crore people under 40 years of age. 
 
• This ambitious goal highlights the program's dedication to reaching a large portion of the population, promoting early diagnosis and intervention.

questions.question: The _______ repeals the Indian Penal Code, 1860 (IPC).
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita Bill**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The Indian Lok Sabha recently passed the Bharatiya Nyaya (Second) Sanhita, 2023 bill to replace the Indian Penal Code (IPC) of 1860. The new bill has included a provision for the death penalty for those guilty of mob lynching.
 
• According to Section 103 (2) of the new bill, any group of five or more persons found guilty of committing murder on the ground of race, caste, community, sex, place of birth, language, personal belief, or any similar ground will face the punishment of death or life imprisonment, in addition to other potential fines.
 
• Union Home Minister Amit Shah has stated in the Lok Sabha that mob lynching is a grave crime, and, in order to deter this practice, the death penalty provision has been included in the new laws.
 
• The new bill has also introduced a specific chapter titled 'Crimes against Women and Children', focusing on sexual crimes. It includes severe punishment for gang rape, with a minimum of 20 years of imprisonment or life sentence being mandated.
 
• The term 'sedition' has been completely removed from the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita Bill. The new legislation, instead, introduces the term 'treason' with focus on acts that endanger 'sovereignty or unity and integrity of India'. The definition of treason includes the mention of 'intent', providing a safeguard for freedom of expression.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The bill further modifies certain language to better represent its legal intentions. Words such as 'hatred' and 'contempt' have been removed and phrases like 'armed rebellion', 'destructive activities', and 'separatist activities' have been included.
 
• Overall, the new Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita includes 358 sections compared to the previous 511 in the IPC.
 
• It adds 21 new offences, increases imprisonment terms for 41 offences, enhances penalties for 82 offences, introduces minimum mandatory punishment for 25 crimes, includes community service as a punishment in 6 crimes, and repeals 19 sections.

questions.question: In India, the Green Revolution was mainly led by _______.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**M.S. Swaminathan**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Green revolution

 
 
• The green revolution refers to the large increase in the production of food grains resulting from the use of high-yielding variety (HYV) seeds, especially for wheat and rice crops.
 
• The first phase of the green revolution took place during the period ranging from the mid-1960s up to the mid-1970s.
 
• During the first phase, the use of HYV seeds was restricted to the more affluent states like Punjab, Andhra Pradesh, and Tamil Nadu. 
 
• During the second phase of the green revolution (the mid-1970s to mid-1980s), the HYV technology spread to a larger number of states and benefitted more variety of crops.
 
• The adoption of green revolution technology enabled India to achieve self-sufficiency in the production of food grains.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Facts about the green revolution

 
 
• ​M.S. Swaminathan is known as the father of the green revolution in India.
 
• The green revolution was a great success and changed India’s status from a food-deficient economy to one of the world’s leading agricultural economies.
 
• The green revolution in India started in the year 1965-68 and lasted till the year 1977-78.
 
 

Thus, the green revolution took place in India in the mid-1960s.

questions.question: Which of the following is the time period of the Tenth Five Year Plan?
questions.solution:

• The plan focused on achieving 8% annual GDP growth.
 
• It emphasized agriculture, infrastructure development, and education as priority sectors.

• It introduced the National Rural Employment Guarantee Act (NREGA) to provide employment to rural households.
 
• The plan also focused on improving the health of the population and increasing access to healthcare services.
 
• It aimed to achieve universal literacy and improve the quality of education at all levels.
 
• The plan was successful in achieving most of its objectives and laid the foundation for subsequent Five-Year Plans.

questions.question: The _______ of a firm during a year ≡ production of the firm during the year - sale of the firm during the year.

options.text: change in inventories and working capitals

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**change of inventories**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• The correct way to express the change of inventories of a firm during a year is by calculating the inventory turnover or by using the formula for the change in inventories.
 
 
• Inventory Turnover:

 
 
• Inventory turnover is a financial ratio that measures the number of times a company's inventory is sold and replaced during a given period.
 
• It is calculated by dividing the cost of goods sold (COGS) by the average inventory value.
 
• The formula for inventory turnover is:
 
 
• Inventory Turnover = Cost of Goods Sold / Average Inventory
 
 
 
 
 
• Change in Inventories::-
 
 
• The change in inventories can be calculated by subtracting the ending inventory value from the beginning inventory value.
 
• The formula for the change in inventories is:
 
 
• Change in Inventories = Ending Inventory - Beginning Inventory
 
• This measure represents the net increase or decrease in inventory over a specific period, such as a year. A positive value indicates an increase in inventory, while a negative value suggests a decrease.

questions.question: A handball team consists of _______ players.

__
 
• Handball is also known as team handball 
 
• It is played by passing a ball using their hands with the aim of throwing it into the goal of the other team.
 
• A standard match consists of two periods of 30 minutes and the team that scores more goals wins.

Explanation:__

Handball team:

__
 
• It is a team sport
 
• It is played between two teams of seven players each (six outcount players and a goalkeeper)

Handball (Dimensions):

 
• According to IHF(International Handball Federation) rule-

 
 
• Length-40m
 
• Breadth-20m
 
• Half diagonal- 28.28
 
• Full diagonal-44.72.
 
• The inner dimension of goal post- 2X3m 
 
• The full dimension of goal post- 2.08 X 3.16m 
 
• Centerline- 20 m from any end line.
 
 

Thus, there are 7 players in a handball team.__

__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

questions.question: India, also known as Bharat, is a:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Union of states**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__** Article 1 of the Constitution of India states that India, or Bharat, shall be a Union of States: 
Article 1(1): *India, that is Bharat, shall be a Union of States.*
Article 1(2): *The States and the territories thereof shall be the States and their territories specified in Parts A, B and C of the First Schedule.*
The territory of India consists of the states, union territories specified in the First Schedule, and other acquired territories. Article 2 states that acquired territories can be converted into states. 
Article 1 is the foundational provision that establishes the Union of India. It sets the tone for the entire constitutional framework of India. 
The name "Bharat" is derived from the name of the Vedic community of Bharatas. It is also said to be derived from the name of either Dushyanta's son Bharata of Mahabharata.

questions.question: Which of the following elements is a part of the P block of the periodic table?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Oxygen**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• In 1869, Russian chemist Dmitri Mendeleev created the framework that became the modern periodic table
 
• He also left gaps for elements that were yet to be discovered.
 
• While arranging the elements according to their atomic weight, if he found that they did not fit into the group he would rearrange them.
 
• British chemist John Newlands was the first to arrange the elements into a periodic table with increasing order of atomic masses.
 
• He arranged the elements in eight groups but left no gaps for undiscovered elements.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Gregor Mendel, through his work on pea plants, discovered the fundamental laws of inheritance.
 
• Mendel tracked the segregation of parental genes and their appearance in the offspring as dominant or recessive traits.
 
• In 1913, Niels Bohr proposed a theory for the hydrogen atom, based on the quantum theory that some physical quantities only take discrete values.
 
• Dalton's atomic theory suggested that all matter was comprised of indivisible and indestructible atoms with distinct masses and properties, the combination of which determined the physical nature of their constituent elements.

Modern Periodic Table -

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.britannica.com/45/7445-050-BB332C27/version-periodic-table-elements.jpg]
